sla_requirements: Uptime target: customer requests 99.99% annual uptime for dedicated pool (requests 4 nines)
Credit schedule: tiered credits by monthly uptime % (>=99.99: 0%, 99.9-99.99: 10%, 99.0-99.9: 25%, <99.0: 50%), wants explicit cap and payout timeline (45 days)
Planned maintenance: prefer one 2-hour monthly maintenance window during 02:00-06:00 local; no more than 6 maintenance events/year without credit
Emergency maintenance: immediate fallback policy + customer notification SLA <= 30 minutes
Support response times: P1 initial ack <= 15 minutes, P1 resolution target 4 hours (workaround) and 24-72 hours for full remediation
Data residency & audit: quarterly audit reports, retain audit logs 2 years, KMS key control by customer (bring-your-own-key optional)
technical_requirements: Throughput guarantees: baseline reserved 8xA100-equivalent GPUs (or specified vGPU units) with 180M token/min sustained for batch embedding pipelines
Burst capacity: optional 2x burstable nodes for traffic spikes (scale up within 90s), billing for burst separate from committed capacity
Latency SLOs: 95th percentile single-turn chat latency <= 120ms for 512-token context on dedicated pool
KV/prefix caching: persistent KV cache across instances for low-latency re-rank flows; require cache warm-start on failover
Model pinning & rollouts: support pinned model versions, canary rollouts with automatic fallback to prior model

They want SLA language that ties credits to monthly invoice; no unilateral maintenance without >72h notice except true emergencies
Legal wants a negotiated cap on aggregate credits (max 12 months of fees) and a termination right if uptime <98% in any 3-month rolling period
